Scenes: @UUID[Compendium.points-of-interest.scenes.Scene.CGaXwOUUH59BdUGA]{09. The Iron Juggernaut}, @UUID[Compendium.points-of-interest.scenes.Scene.proOSKAlcQSKZYb7]{09. The Iron Juggernaut: Cargo Hold}

Actors: @UUID[Compendium.points-of-interest.actors.Actor.BQTJqMAzpuhW85xk]{The Iron Juggernaut}, @UUID[Compendium.points-of-interest.actors.Actor.JrUM4zcUeK2nqIYe]{Brann Kesk}, @UUID[Compendium.points-of-interest.actors.Actor.1uOHJ0yxxLEvB4G0]{Ottilie Kesk}, @UUID[Compendium.points-of-interest.actors.Actor.FWM41aRNbIdGH0jG]{Tarku}

Zone Zone 17: Numeria (grassland scarred by an ancient patrol trench)
Hex 0.4 on the Stolen Lands map
Type Combat + rescue against a starvation clock; linked to @UUID[Compendium.points-of-interest.journals.JournalEntry.dO1SJTMbMCHcThyz.JournalEntryPage.O5rNFDKxgn9WE38b]{#21 The Annihilator}
Threat Moderate 80 XP at party level 16
Creatures Elite Numerian adamantine golem (level 18, Kingmaker), reflavoured as a tracked hauler

Irovetti's map note. A dotted loop drawn around a stretch of plain with an arrow showing the direction of travel. Beside it, written twice: "adamantine — HOW MUCH?" The second time is underlined. A later note in a shakier hand: "salvagers not back."

Background. The Juggernaut is a tracked hauler built to carry cargo to a depot that the Rain of Stars destroyed ten thousand years ago. Its orders never changed. It rolls its loop, reaches the crater where the depot stood, finds no one to receive its load, and turns back for another circuit. One circuit takes three days. The Juggernaut's cargo is living. Annihilators bring their captives to a docking cradle on the loop and transfer them into its hold, and the Juggernaut carries them toward a delivery that never happens. The hold has no stasis, no food and no water. Every captive delivered here starves. The floor is deep in bones, and scratched tallies cover the walls. The longest tally belongs to Tarku, a Kellid hunter delivered a century ago, whose spear still lies with his remains. The newest tally belongs to Brann and Ottilie Kesk, two of Irovetti's salvagers. The Annihilator caught them prying plates off the Juggernaut and delivered them nine days ago. They are still alive.

Arrival.

The ground shakes before you see it. A trench cuts straight across the grassland, and along it grinds a machine the size of a house on two wide tracks, its hull plated in dark grey metal. Steam bleeds from vents along its sides. It doesn't slow as it passes. From somewhere inside comes a slow, weak knocking.

Features.

  • Patrol trench. 12 feet deep and 30 feet wide, with crumbling walls (DC 30 Athletics to Climb). The Juggernaut rolls along the trench floor. Creatures on the rim have standard cover from its vents.
  • Docking cradle. A rusted gantry of girders straddling the trench at the loop's northern bend, where the Annihilator transfers captives. A creature on the gantry can drop onto the Juggernaut's hull as it passes (DC 36 Acrobatics; on a failure, it lands prone in the trench).
  • Depot crater. A glassed bowl at the loop's southern bend. The Juggernaut stops here for 1 minute each circuit, broadcasting a request for a receiving clerk in antique Numerian. This is the one time it stands still.
  • Salvage camp. The Kesks' abandoned camp beside the trench: a toppled wagon (standard cover), pry bars, chains and a cracked plate of adamantine.
  • Cargo hold. Reached through a dorsal hatch (two Interact actions and a DC 38 Thievery check, or DC 38 Athletics to Force Open). Inside: bones, tallies and the Kesks.

Running the encounter.

  • Reading the loop. A PC who watches one full circuit, or succeeds at a DC 36 Survival check to read the trench wear, learns the route, the cradle and the stop at the depot crater. A DC 38 Crafting or Society check on the crater's broadcast reveals the Juggernaut is waiting for a clerk's authorisation code.
  • Inexorable. The Juggernaut never leaves its route and never stops except at the crater. It uses Inexorable March on anything in the trench and Vent (described as a spray of cutting lasers) on creatures on its hull or flanks. It makes fist Strikes with two manipulator arms against boarders. Electricity slows it through Golem Antimagic; acid damages it.
  • Repair Mode. At 0 HP the Juggernaut enters Repair Mode and keeps crawling at Slowed 1 while it uses Self-Repair. The PCs must keep it down, cut its tracks or pull its order core to end the threat for good.
  • The rescue. The PCs don't need to destroy the Juggernaut to save the Kesks. They can board it, open the hold and carry the captives out while it rolls. A boarding party fights the Juggernaut on a moving hull: each round on the hull, a creature must succeed at a DC 32 Acrobatics or Athletics check at the start of its turn or fall prone, and a critical failure throws it into the trench.
  • Starvation clock. The Kesks have 3 days left when the PCs first see the Juggernaut. Each day they lose 1 more point of drained. At 0 days, Brann dies first; Ottilie dies the next day.

Outcomes.

  • Destroyed or disabled. The PCs reach the hold at leisure and recover the Kesks, the adamantine plating and the bones of everyone the annihilators ever delivered.
  • Boarded and rescued. The PCs free the Kesks and leave the Juggernaut rolling. It keeps receiving the Annihilator's captives.
  • Delivery fulfilled. A PC at the depot crater who succeeds at a DC 41 Crafting or Society check (very hard), or speaks antique Numerian and succeeds at a DC 38 Deception check, poses as the receiving clerk. The Juggernaut opens its hold, unloads, and shuts down with its orders complete. On a critical success, the PC can give it a new destination.
  • The Annihilator connection. If the Annihilator still roams, the Juggernaut's hold fills again. Ottilie can describe the four-legged machine that caught them, and the cradle's scorch marks show where it docks.

Rewards. 80 XP, plus 20 XP for each Kesk rescued alive. Treasure: adamantine plating worth 3,000 gp in raw metal, the Kesks' salvage tools (a set of expanded artisan's tools), and Tarku's spear, a stone-tipped weapon wrapped in a Kellid charm, among the bones (a level 16 permanent item of your choice reflavoured as Kellid). Kingdom benefit: a Juggernaut with a new destination hauls Numerian salvage to the PCs' capital, worth 1 Ore commodity each kingdom turn while it runs. The Kesks will work for the kingdom out of gratitude.

Scaling. At party level 18, add the Annihilator docking at the cradle mid-fight. For a weaker party, remove Repair Mode.
